title: Maximum-Length Palindromic Segment

content.problemStatement:
You receive a string s, output a longest contiguous substring that reads identically from left to right and right to left. If several substrings have the largest length, returning any one of them is valid.

Character comparison is case-sensitive. A substring must occupy consecutive positions in s. Aim for O(n^2) time or better.
constraints: s consists of ASCII letters (a-z, A-Z) and digits (0-9) only
Return any one longest palindromic substring when multiple valid answers exist
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]. Example: ["babad"]
content.outputFormat: Single line: JSON-serialised return value (string). Example: "bab"
notes: The judge accepts any substring that is a palindrome and has maximal length for the input.
Character comparison is case-sensitive. Do not normalize or remove characters before searching.
Any one longest palindromic substring is accepted when multiple answers have the same maximal length.

sampleTestCases.explanation: "bab" and "aba" are both palindromes of maximum length 3; returning "bab" is valid.

solution.approach: Use expand-around-center dynamic scanning. Every palindrome has either a single-character center or a two-character center. Expand around every such center while adjacent characters match, and retain the longest interval found. This returns one valid longest palindromic substring and is naturally case-sensitive.
solution.spaceComplexity: O(n) including the returned substring; O(1) auxiliary space.
notes: The implementation uses O(1) auxiliary working space and stores only the returned substring.
Manacher's algorithm can reduce the worst-case time to O(n), but is not required by the stated constraints.

bruteForce.description: Enumerate every substring, test each substring for palindrome symmetry, and keep the longest valid one.
bruteForce.complexity: O(n^3) time and O(n) space for a copied candidate substring, or O(1) extra space with index comparisons.

better.description: Use dynamic programming where dp[i][j] records whether s[i..j] is a palindrome. Build lengths from 1 upward and retain the longest interval.

optimal.description: Expand around every possible palindrome center. For each index, expand once for odd-length palindromes and once for even-length palindromes. Update the best interval whenever a longer palindrome is found.
optimal.complexity: O(n^2) time and O(1) auxiliary space, excluding the returned substring.

hints: A palindrome is determined by matching characters outward from its center.
There are two center types: one character for odd lengths and a gap between two characters for even lengths.
Expand around every center and keep track of the longest interval.
Because the judge accepts any longest palindrome, tie-breaking can be deterministic but need not match a unique expected substring.
followUps: Can you implement Manacher's algorithm to achieve O(n) time?
How would the solution change if the judge required the earliest longest palindrome among ties?
Can the same approach be adapted to return the start and end indices instead of the substring?
learningObjectives: Identify odd and even palindrome centers.
Use center expansion to avoid enumerating all substring pairs explicitly.
Handle case-sensitive and alphanumeric input without normalization.
Reason about O(n^2) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
